critical_steps: Pairwise difference control gives sqrt(E_i) <= (1+sqrt(M)) sqrt(E_j) on each selected measurable block.
Summing all individual frame lower bounds over the partition gives the corrected denominator.
A one-point family with one coefficient 1 and m-1 coefficients 1+sqrt(M) satisfies the pairwise condition with equality and has exact universal weaving lower bound 1.
The source denominator is strictly smaller by 2(m-1)sqrt(M), so its claimed lower bound is strictly too large.
integrity.proof_basis: Hilbert-space Minkowski inequality plus an exact one-point scalar extremal family.
integrity.unproved_limits: Finer family-specific optimal bounds using more than A, M, and m are not classified.

limitations: The result corrects the quantitative lower bound in Theorem 4; it does not dispute the qualitative wovenness conclusion.
The sharp guarantee uses only the theorem's pairwise parameter M and the sum of the individual lower bounds.
No claim is made that this universal bound equals the exact lower weaving bound for every fixed family.

title: The sharp pairwise-difference weaving bound needs a square-root term
